title: What Is Programming?
description: What a program actually is, and why a computer needs such exact instructions.

content.value: A computer is fast, but it never guesses. It does exactly what it is told, in the exact order it is told, and nothing more.

content.real: Telling a friend how to make toast
content.text: A friend fills in the gaps. A computer cannot. Leave out "push the lever" and it waits forever with cold bread. Every step must be there, in the right order.

items: **Programming** is the job of writing those orders down.
A **program** is a list of instructions in a language the computer can be made to understand.
A **bug** is a mistake in a program: usually the computer doing what you wrote, not what you meant.
content.title: Key ideas

content.question: Your program skips a step you forgot to write. What does the computer do?
options: Exactly what you wrote, without the missing step
content.explain: A computer never fills in gaps. It follows the instructions you wrote, even when one is missing.

content.value: Unless you say otherwise, a program runs one line at a time, starting at the top and working down. That one rule explains most of what you will see.

steps.note: The first instruction runs first. It prints `Bread in.`
Then the next line down prints `Lever down.`

content.title: Watch the order
content.intro: Ignore the words `public class Main` for now. Watch only the three instructions in the middle.
content.outro: Three instructions, three lines of output, same order.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: Lines run top to bottom, so `B` prints first. Each `println` ends its line, so `A` goes on the next one.

items.sub: All of them are lists of instructions somebody wrote.
Programming lets you build software, not just use it.

items.text: What you will build in Java
items.sub: A quiz game, a bank machine and a program that tracks money.

steps.label: Change
steps.detail: fix or improve, then run again

content.title: How you will work
content.caption: You cannot break anything. The worst that happens is an error message, and you will learn to read those too.

content.value: Press Run on the editor beside this lesson to see the toast program work.

practice.question: Change the three instructions so the program describes brushing your teeth instead: three steps, in the right order.

quiz.question: What is a program?
options: A list of instructions for a computer to follow.
A machine that thinks for itself.
A picture of what an app should look like.
quiz.explain: A program is instructions, nothing more. The computer supplies the speed; you supply the thinking.

quiz.question: In what order does a program normally run its instructions?
options: Top to bottom, one line at a time.
All at once, in any order.
quiz.explain: By default each line runs after the one above it. Later you will learn how to change that order on purpose, with decisions and loops.

quiz.question: Your program prints the steps of making toast in the wrong order. Whose mistake is it?
options: Yours: the computer ran the order you wrote.
The computer's: it should have worked out the right order.
quiz.explain: The computer never rearranges your instructions to be helpful. If the order is wrong, the order in your code is wrong.
